_comment: The DEFINITION of the production bin grid: the parameters it is derived with, the corpus it is derived from, and a content digest of the result. This file is the single source of those parameters -- helix.data.bins reads its defaults here, and scripts/derive_coeff_bins.py takes its argparse defaults from those, so the numbers live in one place.
name: coeff_bins_r1_tau05_run0027575715_v3

corpus._basis_digest_note: Checkable BEFORE deriving, and catches the pre-tau/r1 confusion. It does NOT identify which run: basis_digest hashes the DSP recipe, so all eight r1 runs share it.
corpus._run_note: Which run cannot be checked from the data. Shard /config carries only band_lengths, gids, n_wires, norm_sigma -- no source-run id -- so the run is knowable only from the directory name. That is why the digests below exist: they are the only thing that detects a grid derived from the wrong run.
corpus._site_note: v3 is recorded against the NERSC copy of the corpus at $CFS/m5238/users/oalter/coeff_tpc_r1/run_0027575715 (19,999 events, 100 coeff + 100 coeff_clean shards, every shard built on a 2080 Ti at helix c646886).

_rerecord_note: v2 named the S3DF corpus and its digests were edges 79485d19, cent_asinh cae984e7, cent_ratio cf3859b7. Deriving with IDENTICAL params from the NERSC corpus -- same run, same basis_digest 8c4542b6, check_corpus ok -- produced all three differently, so the two corpora are not the same bytes and the cause was not established. The grids that v2 fingerprints are the ones the S3DF-published checkpoints were trained against; no such checkpoint was transferred here, and the plan is to retrain, so v3 fingerprints the corpus that will actually be trained on. A number produced here is therefore NOT comparable with a number in docs/SCIENCE.md.
